title: Turnstile oncall bridgeway notes
content:
PURPOSE
Quick, messy bridge notes for Turnstile night/early-morning handoffs. Not a final runbook — use for immediate triage and context. Meant to be pasted into Slack thread and appended to weekly incident notes.

CONTEXT SUMMARY
- Service: turnstile (request router + model-mux for hosted API)
- Common symptoms: increased 5xxs on model-proxy, long tail latency for streaming responses, cache-miss storms after deploys
- Current normal: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms, error budget: 99.9% uptime SLA on hosted endpoints
- Recent changes: routing policy tweak (weight shift to dedicated pool alpha) deployed 2024-11-06 (RDW-2345). Watch for spillover to fallback models.

ACTIVE ITEMS (check these first when taking bridge)
1) Alerts to scan: turnstile:5xx-rate, turnstile:kv-cache-miss-spike, turnstile:worker-saturation, turnstile:ff-stream-error
2) Open incidents: none (as of handoff). If one exists, paste the incident summary here and ping pager.
3) Ongoing experiment: weight-split-rr to dedicated-alpha (10% traffic). If you see capacity alerts on dedicated-alpha, rollback weight to 0% and notify infra.

QUICK TRIAGE FLOWS (one-liners to run on first sign)
- If 5xx spike: check svc logs -> `kubectl -n turnstile logs -l app=model-proxy --tail 200` and identify 500 vs 502 vs 504.
- If proxy 502/connection refused: likely model backend down. Check pods: `k get pods -n models -l model=llama-13b -o wide` then `k describe pod` for OOM / CrashLoop backtrace.
- If latency p95 rises but error rate stable: look at batching/backpressure and KV cache hitrate: Grafana dashboard "Turnstile - serving runtime" -> panel: kv_cache_hit_ratio. If < 0.6, suspect cache eviction after deploy.
- If cache miss storm after deploy: run cache-warm script (ops-only) -> `scripts/warm_cache.sh --model llama-13b --prefixes /opt/warm/prompts.txt` (temporary, runs from bastion; ask SRE for elevated token).

FALLBACKS / SHORT-TERM MITIGATIONS
- Model fallback: route to quantized variant if native model OOMs (e.g., llama-13b -> llama-13b-q8). Command (console): set routing rule `turnstile.routing.setFallback(\"llama-13b\",\"llama-13b-q8\")` (requires console role).
- Reduce batch size: temp override in route config: set `max_batch_tokens` -> 4096 (down from 8192) to reduce latency spikes.
- Disable streaming: if streaming errors dominate, flip route to non-streaming for impacted route to avoid partial payload hangups.

RESTARTS / PATCH PLAYBOOKS (order matters)
1) Restart model-proxy (graceful): `k rollout restart deployment/model-proxy -n turnstile` (safe to do during low traffic windows).
2) If model pods are CrashLoopBackoff across nodes: cordon node, drain (one-by-one) to force re-sched; check for node oom or driver issues. Contact infra oncall before node-level actions.
3) Rolling restart of model workers: use `kubectl rollout status` and watch queue length. Avoid simultaneous restart of all workers for same model.

COMMUNICATION (copy-paste snippets)
- Incident open (small): "Opening: elevated 5xxs on turnstile (p95 latency). Investigating model-proxy and KV cache. Will update in 15m. Assigned: @oncall. Jira RDW-XXXX created."
- Hotfix notice: "Hotfix: reduced routing weight to dedicated-alpha (10%->0%). Rolling back to reduce pressure on dedicated pool; monitoring for 5xx drop."

SHORT COMMAND CHEAT SHEET
- k get pods -n turnstile
- k logs -f podname -n turnstile --container=model-proxy
- curl -v $TURNSTILE_HEALTH/health (replace env var in bastion)
- tail -n 500 /var/log/turnstile/proxy.log on bastion

POST-HANDOFF CHECKLIST (what to leave for next person)
- Note any throttles I applied and why (routing weight, batch overrides).
- If I restarted pods, list pod names and start times.
- If I ran cache-warm, attach the warm logs or S3 link.
- Outstanding TODOs with priority: bugfix PRs to revert temp overrides (HIGH).

KNOWN GOTTCHAS / REMINDERS
- Dedicated pool alpha sometimes reports false capacity available due to the autoscaler bug (RDW-2171). If autoscaler reports free GPUs but pods don't schedule, escalate to infra.
- Model-variant naming: q8 suffix indicates 8-bit quant; q4 names are sometimes incompatible with the runtime if compiled kernels not present (watch errors: \"unsupported quantization path\").
- Never restart the qps-aggregator service during blue-green deploys (leads to 30s blips).

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF
- Follow up with Applied ML: confirm whether we can pre-warm embeddings cache during deploys (impact on startup).
- Investigate: frequent sample of 504s at 03:00 UTC — correlates with logs rotation? (check logrotate config on bastion)

BACKUPS & ARTIFACTS (where to find evidence)
- Grafana: team dashboard -> Turnstile - serving runtime
- Kibana: index turnstile-* -> filter by request_id or path
- S3: s3://turnstile-ops/warm-logs/YYYYMMDD/*

TODO (short-term)
- [ ] Draft a small runbook for cache-warm (move script to ops repo and add RBAC note) — owner: Aisha (this week).
- [ ] Add a canned Slack alert for fallback activation (so product knows when quality drops).

SIGN-OFF (handoff script)
- If you're taking bridge now: confirm you can access bastion and console, check alerts, and run the quick triage flows for any active alert. If you need help, ping #sre-turnstile and tag Jonah/Kim.

END NOTES
- This doc is intentionally terse. Keep a fresh copy in incident notes when you open an incident (paste timestamped).
- If you make changes to reroutes or batch settings, append a single-line summary here with timestamp so the next bridge sees state immediately.

paste example entry (for next person)
"2024-12-02 02:17 UTC — reduced dedicated-alpha weight 10->0 due to node oom; warmed cache for llama-13b; restarted model-proxy deployment (model-proxy-5 -> model-proxy-6). Monitoring p95. Aisha."
